title: Monomial etale charts of regular log-smooth schemes over a trait
statement:
A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal; a uniformizer $\pi$ is a generator of that maximal ideal.

Use fs log structures, charts and log morphisms as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The canonical log structure on a trait is the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_S$ of sections invertible on its generic point; a uniformizer gives its chart $\mathbf N\to R$. In this statement, log smooth over that trait has its fs chart meaning: etale locally on source and target there are compatible charts $\mathbf N\to P$ with $P$ fine saturated, the group map injective with torsion in its cokernel of finite order invertible on the source, such that the induced scheme map to $S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ is smooth. Here $\mathbf Z[P]$ is the free abelian group on $P$ with multiplication induced by the monoid law.

Let $(X,M)\to S$ be such an fs log-smooth morphism with $X$ regular Noetherian [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every point $x\in X$ and every uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$, there exist a regular affine Noetherian scheme $U$, an etale morphism $a:U\to X$, a point $u\in U$ with $a(u)=x$, an integer $n\geq1$, nonnegative integers $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ not all zero, and an etale $S$-morphism
$$b:U\longrightarrow T=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(T_1^{e_1}\cdots T_n^{e_n}-\pi)\bigr).$$
Here etale has the meaning of [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $\operatorname{Spec}$ is [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.6.5, printed p.253, using Proposition 3.6.3, printed p.252; canonical trait log structure in Definition 3.6.1.

proof.text: The canonical log trait is log regular. At a geometric point over the closed point, let $A$ be its strict local ring. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension], $A$ is Noetherian of dimension one; [lem-sc-ring-strict-henselization-local-maximal-ideal] identifies its maximal ideal with $(\pi)$. Thus its characteristic is $\mathbf N$, its nonunit log ideal is $(\pi)$, and its stratum ring is the residue field. At a geometric point over the generic point the ordinary local ring is a field, and the same maximal-ideal statement gives zero maximal ideal in its strict henselization. The log structure is trivial there, its characteristic has rank zero, and its strict local ring is a field. These are exactly the stratum regularity and dimension equalities of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: Expose XVI Definition 3.6.1, p.252; VI 1.2, p.69. Strict henselization inputs: Stacks Tags 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian), 06LK (lemma-henselization-dimension), 04GP (lemma-strict-henselization), maximal-ideal clause.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-log-smooth-invertible-torsion-log-regular] to $(X,M)\to S$: source and target are locally Noetherian fs, Step 1 proves the target log regular, and the injective chart group map, invertible torsion order, and smooth comparison are exactly the hypotheses assumed for $(X,M)\to S$. Hence $(X,M)$ is log regular. Fix $x\in X$ and choose an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], giving a geometric point $\bar x$ over $x$ as in [def-weil-geometric-point]. Since $X$ is regular, [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] gives an isomorphism $\overline M_{\bar x}\cong\mathbf N^r$ for some $r\geq0$. Only its pointwise equivalence is used, not its boundary conclusion.

source.place: Expose VI 1.7--1.8, p.70; XVI Proposition 3.6.5, third paragraph, p.253.

proof.text: Keep the specified chart $Q=\mathbf N\to R$, $1\mapsto\pi$. This monoid is fs with torsion-free group completion $\mathbf Z$: a positive multiple of an integer is nonnegative only if that integer is nonnegative. The assumed compatible injective charts make $(X,M)\to S$ log smooth in [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Apply [lem-per-log-smooth-differential-generators] at $\bar x$ with this fixed base chart. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$, $D=A^\times$, and $C=B/D$. Obtain $t_1,\ldots,t_d\in M_{\bar x}$ and $m\geq1$ invertible in $A$ such that the $d\log t_i$ are a basis of the relative logarithmic differential module. The lemma also gives $C$ torsion-free, $D$ $m$-divisible, and finite cokernel killed by $m$ for $L=\mathbf Z^d\oplus\mathbf Z\to C$. This map sends $(a,q)$ to the class of $\sum a_it_i+f^\flat(q)$, writing $B$ additively. No replacement of the trait or its uniformizer is made.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, first half, p.252, with fixed Q=N; Definition 3.6.1.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:L\to B$ send $(a,q)$ to $\sum a_it_i+f^\flat(q)$. Apply [lem-per-divisible-unit-lattice-extension] with $n=m$, this finite free group $L$, and subgroup $D=A^\times$. Step 3 supplies each hypothesis: $D$ is $m$-divisible, $B/D$ is torsion-free, and $(B/D)/\operatorname{im}(L)$ is finite and killed by $m$. Thus there are a finite free abelian group $G$, an injection $i:L\to G$, and $h:G\to B$ extending $\varphi$, with $G/i(L)$ killed by a power of $m$ and $G\to C$ surjective. These maps and the differential basis from Step 3 are fixed for the chart construction.

source.place: Expose XVI Lemma 3.6.4, pp.252--253, used in the proof of Proposition 3.6.3.

proof.text: Set $P=h^{-1}(M_{\bar x})\subseteq G$. Apply [lem-per-kato-lattice-chart-realization] with $Q=\mathbf N$, the basis from Step 3, and the maps from Step 4. The source and target are locally Noetherian fs and log smooth; $Q^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free, $m$ is invertible in $A$, and Step 4 gives the required extension, finite-index condition and characteristic surjectivity. Obtain a pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)\to(X,\bar x)$, this fs monoid $P$ with $P^{\rm gp}=G$, its chart, and an etale comparison $c:V\to Z=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$. The base chart remains $1\mapsto\pi$ and the compatible monoid map is $q\mapsto i(0,q)$. It is injective since $i$ is; $P^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free since $G$ is free. The pointed neighbourhood gives a geometric lift of $\bar x$. The restriction-stalk colimit of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and strict-local invariance [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identify the log stalks and their unit groups. Hence the characteristic at $\bar v$ is the $\mathbf N^r$ from Step 2.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3, last paragraph, p.252, followed by Proposition 3.6.5, first paragraph, p.253.

proof.text: Let $F\subset P$ be the elements whose structural functions are units at $\bar v$. The localized-chart theorem [lem-trf-chart-face-localization-logification] says that $F$ is a face and, putting $P_F=\{p-f:p\in P,f\in F\}$ and $H=F^{\rm gp}$, identifies $P_F/H$ with $\overline M_{\bar x}$. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening], $P_F$ is fs with unit group $H$, and the sharpening has finite free group completion. These statements apply to the given chart, including any units it already has; no sharpness of $P$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.5, first two paragraphs, p.253; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, pp.98--99.

proof.text: Choose finite generators $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ of $P$. The face $F$ is generated by those $p_j$ which lie in $F$: a sum lying in a face has every summand in the face. Restrict $V$ to the open neighbourhood $V_0$ where these finitely many structural functions are units. The chart extends to $P_F$ there. Algebraically $\mathbf Z[P_F]$ is $\mathbf Z[P]$ with the corresponding monomials inverted: a map out of either ring is precisely a monoid map from $P$ taking $F$ to units. Thus the new comparison target $Z_F=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P_F]$ is the open in $Z$ where those monomials are units, and $V_0=c^{-1}(Z_F)$. The inverse-image equality is also the principal-open formula in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Its comparison is etale: its composite with the open immersion to $Z$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2), and cancellation (3) applies.

Use [lem-trf-integral-monoid-free-sharpening-splitting] for the integral monoid $P_F$. Its sharpening is $\mathbf N^r$ by Steps 2 and 6, with group completion $\mathbf Z^r$. Obtain a monoid isomorphism $P_F\cong\mathbf N^r\oplus H$, restricting to the identity on the unit group. The group $P^{\rm gp}$ is finite free: its finite monoid generators generate the group, so use [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure] and torsion-freeness to eliminate its finite primary factors. The subgroup theorem [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] therefore gives a finite basis of $H\subset P^{\rm gp}$, say $a_1,\ldots,a_s$.

Write the image of $1\in\mathbf N$ in $P_F\cong\mathbf N^r\oplus H$ as $(e_1,\ldots,e_r,h)$, with $e_i\geq0$. Write $h=\sum_j f_ja_j$. Replacing each $a_j$ with $-a_j$ when its coefficient is negative makes all $f_j\geq0$. The vector $(e_1,\ldots,e_r,f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ is nonzero: otherwise the image of $1$ in $P_F$ would equal the image of $0$, contradicting the injection $\mathbf N\to P$ and the inclusion $P_F\subset P^{\rm gp}$. In particular $n=r+s\geq1$. This argument also covers $r=0$ (a point over the generic fibre): then a nonzero coordinate in the group factor supplies a positive exponent.

Under the chosen monoid isomorphism, $\mathbf Z[P_F]=\mathbf Z[t_1,\ldots,t_r,z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_s^{\pm1}]$: monoid basis elements correspond bijectively to ordinary monomials in $t_i$ and Laurent monomials in $z_j$, respecting multiplication. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Z_F$ has ring $R\otimes_{\mathbf Z[q]}\mathbf Z[P_F]$, where $q\mapsto\pi$ in $R$ and $q\mapsto\prod_i t_i^{e_i}\prod_jz_j^{f_j}$ in the other factor. Its universal property is therefore that of $R[t_i,z_j^{\pm1}]/(\prod_i t_i^{e_i}\prod_jz_j^{f_j}-\pi)$. It is precisely the localization at $\prod_jz_j$ of the monomial hypersurface ring $R[t_i,z_j]/(\prod_i t_i^{e_i}\prod_jz_j^{f_j}-\pi)$; maps from both sides specify the same coordinates, the same relation, and invertible $z_j$. Thus $Z_F$ is an open subscheme of the required $T$ (if $s=0$ this is the whole scheme). The comparison followed by this open immersion is an etale $S$-map by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

It remains to choose the required regular affine neighbourhood. Since $X$ is regular, [def-weil-regular-scheme] supplies a regular Noetherian affine open $X_1$ containing $x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] to $V\to X$ and the open $V_0\cap a^{-1}(X_1)$, at $\bar v$. It gives an affine open $U$ containing its image, and $a:U\to X$ etale. The restricted $U\to T$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The affine morphism $U\to X_1$ is smooth, since it is etale; use the affine-local smooth-ring interpretation explicitly included in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] applied to their coordinate rings shows that the ring of $U$ is regular (and Noetherian). Thus $U$ is regular affine Noetherian. Its marked point $u$ maps to $x$. Steps 9--10 supply the required nonzero exponent vector and the required etale $S$-map, for the originally specified uniformizer.

lean.statement:
theorem regular_logSmooth_monomial_chart
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1) (π : R)
    (hπ : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R = Ideal.span {π})
    (M : EtaleLogStructure (Spec (.of R))) (hfs : M.IsFineSaturated)
    (hcanonical : ∃ e : M.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf
        ((Spec (.of R)).basicOpen ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv π)).ι,
      e.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap
        ((Spec (.of R)).basicOpen ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv π)).ι = M.alpha)
    (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (hregular : IsRegularScheme X.scheme)
    [IsNoetherian X.scheme] (x : X.scheme)
    (f : EtaleLogHom X ⟨Spec (.of R), inferInstance, M, hfs⟩)
    (hcharts : ∀ y : X.scheme, ∃ c : FSLogChart f,
      y ∈ Set.range c.V.hom ∧
      ∃ e : c.P ≃* Multiplicative (ULift.{u} ℕ),
        (∃ π₀ : R, IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R = Ideal.span {π₀} ∧
          ∀ p : c.P, M.alpha.app (op c.W) (c.chartY p) =
            c.W.hom.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv π₀) ^ (e p).toAdd.down) ∧
        Function.Injective c.groupMap ∧ Finite (CommGroup.torsion c.cokernel) ∧
        (∀ v : c.V.left,
          IsUnit (Nat.card (CommGroup.torsion c.cokernel) : c.V.left.presheaf.stalk v)) ∧
        Smooth c.comparison) :
    ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (a : U ⟶ X.scheme) (v : U),
      IsAffine U ∧ IsRegularScheme U ∧ IsNoetherian U ∧ Etale a ∧ a v = x ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n → ℕ), 0 < n ∧ (∃ i, e i ≠ 0) ∧
        ∃ b : U ⟶ Spec (.of (monomialTraitAlgebra R π n e)), Etale b ∧
          b ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (monomialTraitAlgebraMap R π n e)) =
            a ≫ f.base
